level1.text: The period of a weight oscillating on a spring is $0.40\,\text{s}$. What is the frequency of the oscillation?
A guitar string vibrates at the frequency $196\,\text{Hz}$. What is the period of the vibration of the string? Give the answer in milliseconds.
The graph shows the displacement of a weight oscillating on a spring as a function of time. What is the amplitude of the oscillation?
The pendulum of a pendulum clock makes $20$ full swings in $36\,\text{s}$. What is the period of the pendulum?
A weight oscillates on a spring, and the amplitude of the oscillation is $4.0\,\text{cm}$. How far does the weight travel during one period?
The period of weight A is $0.25\,\text{s}$ and the frequency of weight B is $3.0\,\text{Hz}$. Which weight makes more oscillations per second?
level1.answer: Weight A, because the frequency $4.0\,\text{Hz}$ corresponding to its period is greater than $3.0\,\text{Hz}$.

choices.text: Weight B, because the number $3.0$ is greater than the number $0.25$.
choices.feedback: The period and the frequency cannot be compared by their numerical values, because they are different quantities in different units. The period must first be converted into a frequency $f = \tfrac{1}{T}$.

choices.text: Weight B, because its period $0.33\,\text{s}$ is longer, and a longer period means faster oscillation.
choices.feedback: A longer period means slower oscillation: one oscillation takes more time, so fewer of them fit into a second.

choices.text: They oscillate equally fast, because $0.25\,\text{s}$ and $3.0\,\text{Hz}$ are the same thing in different units.
choices.feedback: They describe the same phenomenon, but they are different quantities, and $0.25\,\text{s}$ corresponds to the frequency $4.0\,\text{Hz}$, not to $3.0\,\text{Hz}$.

choices.text: Weight A, because the frequency $4.0\,\text{Hz}$ corresponding to its period is greater than $3.0\,\text{Hz}$.
choices.feedback: Correct: the frequency is the reciprocal of the period, so $f_A = \tfrac{1}{0.25\,\text{s}} = 4.0\,\text{Hz}$. Weight A makes four oscillations per second, weight B three.

level1.text: The frequency of an oscillator is $1.6\,\text{Hz}$. How long does it take before it has made $40$ full oscillations?
A student claims: “When the frequency of an oscillator doubles, the period also doubles, because both tell about the speed of the oscillation.” Which of the following corrects the claim correctly?
level1.answer: The period is halved, because then only half of the previous time is left for one oscillation.

choices.text: The period doubles, because the period and the frequency are directly proportional.
choices.feedback: They are not directly proportional but reciprocals of each other. When there are twice as many oscillations per second, one oscillation must last a shorter time.

choices.text: The period does not change, because it is a fixed property of the oscillator.
choices.feedback: The period is the duration of one oscillation, and it changes when the frequency changes. It is not a constant but $T = \tfrac{1}{f}$.

choices.text: The period is halved, because then only half of the previous time is left for one oscillation.
choices.feedback: Correct: when $f$ doubles, $T = \tfrac{1}{f}$ is halved. The student mixed up the quantities: faster oscillation means a greater frequency but a shorter period.

choices.text: The period grows slightly, because there are more oscillations and they take more time in total.
choices.feedback: The period is the duration of one oscillation, not the total of all of them. When more oscillations fit into a second, each of them must be shorter.

level2.text: A cart on an air track is attached between two springs and oscillates along the track. The graph shows the displacement of the cart from the equilibrium position as a function of time according to the sine model. What is the displacement of the cart from the equilibrium position at the time $0.10\,\text{s}$?

The sine fit $y = A \sin(Bt + C) + D$ of Graphical Analysis Pro gave the coefficient $B = 12.6\,\tfrac{1}{\text{s}}$ for the measurement of an oscillating weight. What is the frequency of the oscillation?
The needle of a sewing machine moves up and down $900$ times a minute. What is the period of the motion of the needle? Give the answer in milliseconds.

A motion sensor measures the distance to a weight oscillating on a spring. The smallest measured distance is $32.0\,\text{cm}$ and the greatest $47.0\,\text{cm}$. What is the amplitude of the oscillation?

A motion sensor measured the position of a weight oscillating on a spring, and the times of successive peaks of the graph were read into a table (example data).

What is the frequency of the oscillation? Use the whole measurement series.

level2.text:
A student measured the period of a pendulum by timing $10$ full swings by hand five times (example data).

a) Calculate the period of the pendulum from the mean of the measurements.

b) Estimate the uncertainty of the period as half of the range of the measurement results and explain why timing $10$ swings gives a more accurate period than timing one swing.

Write the result of part a) in the answer box.

From a graph of a motion sensor, the moments were read at which a weight oscillating on a spring passes the equilibrium position (example data).

A student calculated: “Successive passes are $0.37\,\text{s}$ apart, so the period is $0.37\,\text{s}$ and the frequency $2.7\,\text{Hz}$.”

Explain the student’s mistake and calculate the correct frequency. Write the correct frequency in the answer box.

data.caption: Passes of the equilibrium position (example data)

level3.text: A weight oscillates sinusoidally with the period $1.2\,\text{s}$, and timing starts when it passes the equilibrium position going up. How long does it take before the weight is for the first time at half the amplitude above the equilibrium position?

A button is fixed to a disc rotating in a vertical plane at $15\,\text{cm}$ from the axis, and the disc rotates uniformly at $45$ revolutions per minute.

The disc is lit from the side by horizontal, parallel light coming from far away, so the shadow of the button moves up and down on the wall beside it.

How far from the middle of its motion is the shadow $0.20\,\text{s}$ after it passed the middle going up?

Two weights oscillate side by side on different springs. The period of the first is $0.60\,\text{s}$ and that of the second $0.90\,\text{s}$. Both pass the equilibrium position going up at the same moment. How soon after that do they next pass the equilibrium position going up at the same time? The oscillation does not die out.

In an electrocardiogram each heartbeat shows up as a sharp R peak. The table gives the times of the R peaks of the same person at rest and right after exercise, six successive beat intervals in each case (example data). The beats repeat approximately evenly, so they can be treated as periodic motion whose period is the beat interval.

a) Determine the beat interval at rest and after exercise from the total time of six intervals and calculate the pulse, that is, the number of beats per minute, in both situations.

b) By how many percent did the pulse rise during exercise?

c) Explain why the period should be determined from the total time of six intervals and not from one beat interval.

Write the result of part b) in the answer box.

data.caption: Times of the R peaks (example data)

level3.text:
A motion sensor measures the distance $d$ to a weight oscillating vertically on a spring. The table is example data: the measurement starts at the time $t = 0$, when the weight passes the equilibrium position and the distance starts to increase. Assume that the oscillation is sinusoidal and does not damp.

a) Read from the table the distance of the equilibrium position $D$, the amplitude $A$ and the period $T$.

b) Model the distance with the expression $d = D + A \sin\left(\tfrac{2\pi t}{T}\right)$ and predict the distance at the time $t = 5.0\,\text{s}$.

c) The measurement covers only one period. Explain why the reliability of the prediction depends on how accurately the period is known.

Write the result of part b) in the answer box.

data.caption: Distance to the motion sensor (example data)
